claims.claim_text: Memory-preserving research agents should be evaluated by proof behavior, not answer correctness alone.
Claim-Score, Evidence-Score, Boundary-Score, Lineage-Score, Promotion-Score, and Notary-Readiness are proposed benchmark dimensions.
Existing NeuroAI and neuromorphic benchmarks show the value of shared evaluation infrastructure.
claims.note: Supported as benchmark precedent, not proof that Proof Scores are valid.

claims.claim_text: Proof Scores can become useful for evaluating agent epistemic conduct.
claims.note: Requires datasets, baselines, inter-rater review, and external validation.

claims.claim_text: The included code, schema, and notebook implement a starter reproducibility scaffold.
claims.note: Only claims file existence and starter functionality, not benchmark validity.

claims.claim_text: Proof Scores are accepted NeuroAI benchmarks or empirically proven superior.
Proof Scores should map to general research-agent risks rather than Medina-only packet style compliance.
claims.note: Maps metrics to status calibration, grounding, inhibition, continuity, state-transition judgment, and integrity-language precision.

claims.claim_text: A mature seed suite should include non-Medina corpora such as open-source project histories, scientific review packets, clinical-trial summaries, grant drafts, reproducibility packages, and conflicting literature reviews.
claims.note: Implemented here as starter task design; still requires validation and external review.

claims.claim_text: This archive implements the five-stage seed build: expanded seed suite, deterministic checks, expert-panel guide, baseline protocol, and public-release checklist.
claims.note: Claims artifact existence and seed functionality, not empirical validation.
